summary: The tools component is the act stage of the loop: ToolRegistry holds every Tool (implementing name/description/schema/execute) as critical (always active) or deferred (discovered via ToolSearchTool), and the built-in tool families give the loop its hands — file editing (FileRead/FileWrite/FileEdit/PatchApply), command execution (ShellExec/PtySession), verification (CargoTest/CargoCheck/CargoClippy), search (GrepSearch/GlobFind/SymbolSearch), version control (GitStatus/GitDiff/GitCheckpoint), containers, browsers, vision, LSP, knowledge graph, and self-introspection. Every act transition on the loop is a registry.execute through this component; its search index, safety configs, and metadata decide which tools the reason stage even gets to see each turn.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with src/tools/ read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in the Tool trait, ToolRegistry register_critical/register_deferred/activate/critical_definitions, tool_search.rs, and the concrete tool modules (file, shell_exec, grep_search, cargo, git, container, pty_shell, vision, lsp_tools, knowledge, introspect, analyzer, hot_reload, task_focus, net_policy).

examples.title: Register critical tools as always-on act nodes
examples.intent: Guarantee core file and shell tools are callable from the first Executing turn without a discovery round-trip.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolRegistry::register_critical activates a Tool immediately and includes it in critical_definitions, so the reason stage always sees file_read/file_write/shell_exec/grep_search in the per-turn tool list and the act stage can dispatch them directly.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drag a tool node from the palette onto the always-on shelf pinned beside the act stage.
touch_interaction.visual: Critical tools render solid with an anchor badge; they never dim or fold away when the shelf collapses.

examples.mini_scenario: On startup the registry pre-registers FileRead and ShellExec as critical; the first Executing turn calls file_read directly, no tool_search needed.
examples.pitfall: Registering too many tools as critical bloats critical_definitions and burns context budget on every reason turn.

examples.title: Defer niche tools behind tool_search
examples.intent: Keep rarely-used tools out of the prompt until the loop actually needs them.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolRegistry::register_deferred adds a Tool without activating it; it is absent from critical_definitions until ToolSearchTool finds it and ToolRegistry::activate flips it on, shrinking per-turn context at the cost of one discovery turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the tool_search hub to fan out deferred tools as ghosted nodes waiting to be summoned.
touch_interaction.visual: Deferred nodes render translucent; on activate they snap to full opacity with a pop and join the act rail.

examples.mini_scenario: The model calls tool_search('container'), the registry returns ContainerRun, and activate makes it callable on the next act turn.
examples.pitfall: Marking a genuinely core tool deferred forces an extra tool_search turn — wasted budget every task that needs it.

examples.title: Discover a tool via the search index
examples.intent: Let the model find the right tool by intent instead of memorizing the full catalog.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolSearchTool::execute queries the shared search index and returns ToolSearchResult entries (name, description, schema, category via categorize_tool); the model perceives the match and acts on the discovered tool next turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the search node to open a query field; matching tools appear as candidate nodes you can drag onto the canvas.
touch_interaction.visual: Candidates glow by relevance; the top match pulses brightest and its category tag colors the edge.

examples.mini_scenario: A task needs container control; the model searches 'run container', gets ContainerRun, and calls it next turn.
examples.pitfall: Returning too many low-relevance ToolSearchResults floods the context and dilutes the model's tool choice.

examples.title: Read before you write with the file tool family
examples.intent: Ground an edit in actual file content before mutating anything.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: FileRead (and DirectoryTree for orientation) feeds the reason stage the current bytes; FileEdit/FileMultiEdit/PatchApply then mutate with old_string anchoring, so each act transition is evidence-backed rather than speculative.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge from the FileRead node's output port into the FileEdit node's input port to enforce read-before-write.
touch_interaction.visual: The edge pulses green when fresh content flows; an edit attempted with no read edge flashes an amber 'unanchored' warning.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop reads config.rs, the model quotes the exact old_string from that ToolResult, and FileEdit applies cleanly on the first try.
examples.pitfall: Editing from memory instead of a fresh FileRead result makes old_string matching fail and wastes a recovery turn.

examples.title: Bound shell commands with safety config and timeouts
examples.intent: Let the loop run arbitrary commands without letting any one command hang or blast the workspace.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ShellExec wraps each command with timeout and safety checks (default_shell, init_safety_config on the file tools follows the same pattern), so the act stage is guarded: a hung command dies at the deadline and returns a typed error instead of stalling the driver.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the ShellExec node to open its gate panel showing timeout, working dir, and safety policy.
touch_interaction.visual: A countdown ring shrinks around the node while the command runs; the ring flashes red one tick before the timeout kills it.

examples.mini_scenario: The model runs a build that deadlocks; ShellExec's timeout fires at 120s, returns an error ToolResult, and the loop recovers instead of hanging.
examples.pitfall: An unbounded ShellExec turns one bad command into a frozen loop — never bypass the timeout for convenience.

examples.title: Grep the codebase as cheap perceive
examples.intent: Locate symbols and call sites without loading whole files into context.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: GrepSearch::grep_search returns GrepMatch lines (path, line, snippet) packed into a GrepSearchResult; the reason stage gets precise coordinates for a few hundred tokens instead of reading entire files, protecting the budget for actual work.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread over the GrepSearch node to fan its matches out as a scatter of file chips, each pinned to a line number.
touch_interaction.visual: Match chips glow by hit density; tapping one jumps the canvas camera to that file's read node.

examples.mini_scenario: The model greps 'fn execute' across src/tools, gets 12 GrepMatch lines, and reads only the two files that matter.
examples.pitfall: Grepping with an over-broad regex returns thousands of matches and truncates — the pagination info must be honored, not ignored.

examples.title: Close the loop with cargo test as verify
examples.intent: Prove an edit compiles and passes before the loop claims completion.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CargoTest parses cargo JSON messages into TestResult/TestSummary with FailureDetail entries; CargoCheck and CargoClippy surface CompilerError by Severity. The verify stage gets structured pass/fail evidence that decides Completed vs ErrorRecovery.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the CargoTest node to expand its TestSummary: green passed count, red failed list with FailureDetail chips.
touch_interaction.visual: The node border seals green on all-pass; each failure renders a red chip that links back to the offending file node.

examples.mini_scenario: After FileEdit lands, CargoTest runs: 41 passed, 1 failed — the FailureDetail routes the loop back to act on the broken test.
examples.pitfall: Trusting the edit without running CargoCheck/CargoTest lets the loop declare Completed on broken code — verify is not optional.

examples.title: Group test failures with the error analyzer
examples.intent: Turn a wall of errors into a prioritized fix list instead of thrashing one at a time.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ErrorAnalyzer::group_by_cause clusters errors into ErrorGroup buckets, prioritize and most_actionable rank them, and suggest_fix proposes next moves — the reason stage converts verify output into one coherent plan rather than N disconnected recovery attempts.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the failure scatter to cluster errors into ErrorGroup buckets by root cause.
touch_interaction.visual: Scattered red chips magnetize into labeled clusters; the most_actionable cluster lifts to the front with a 'fix first' badge.

examples.mini_scenario: Twelve clippy errors cluster into two ErrorGroups — one missing import, one lifetime — and the loop fixes the import once instead of six times.
examples.pitfall: Treating each failure as independent re-derives the same root cause repeatedly; group first, then plan.

examples.title: Checkpoint the repo before a risky act
examples.intent: Create a rollback anchor before the loop mutates many files.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: GitCheckpoint snapshots the working tree before a batch of edits; GitStatus and GitDiff give the verify stage a readout of what actually changed, so a failed batch can roll back to the checkpoint instead of leaving half-applied state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap a checkpoint marker to offer 'restore to here', routing the loop back to that snapshot.
touch_interaction.visual: An anchor badge drops onto the timeline on save; it glows blue while armed as the active restore target.

examples.mini_scenario: Before a FileMultiEdit across eight files the loop runs GitCheckpoint; when three edits fail verify, it restores and retries with a smaller batch.
examples.pitfall: Checkpointing after the mutation is useless — the snapshot must precede the first write in the batch.

examples.title: Isolate an experiment in a git worktree
examples.intent: Let the loop try a risky refactor without touching the main working tree.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EnterWorktreeTool creates an isolated WorktreeEntry and switches the loop's file operations into it; is_in_worktree/get_current_worktree scope later acts, and ExitWorktreeTool returns — the loop's blast radius shrinks to the worktree until results are verified.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drag a plan-step node onto the worktree sandbox to re-scope all its downstream acts into the isolated tree.
touch_interaction.visual: A dashed sandbox ring surrounds the worktree cluster; nodes inside tint violet and their edges stop at the ring boundary.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop enters a worktree, rewrites the parser, runs CargoTest green, then exits and applies the verified diff to main.
examples.pitfall: Running file tools while is_in_worktree is false (thinking you're isolated) mutates the real tree — check the scope before acting.

examples.title: Drive an interactive REPL through a PTY session
examples.intent: Handle tools that need a live session (debuggers, REPLs, ssh) instead of one-shot commands.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PtySession keeps state across turns: send_command writes, read_output collects CommandOutput, is_alive guards reuse, close terminates. The loop's act stage becomes multi-turn conversational against one process instead of spawning a fresh shell per call.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the PtyShellTool node to open its live terminal card showing the session transcript.
touch_interaction.visual: The node shows a breathing 'alive' dot while is_alive is true; output streams in as ticker text under the node.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop starts a Python REPL in a PtySession, sends three expressions across three turns, reads outputs, and closes the session cleanly.
examples.pitfall: Forgetting close leaks PTY processes; every opened session must have a matching close on the loop's exit path.

examples.title: Gate outbound URLs through network policy
examples.intent: Stop web tools from hitting internal hosts or disallowed endpoints.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: NetworkPolicy::validate_url_target (with is_private_or_internal_ip / is_private_network_host) vets every HttpRequest and browser fetch before it executes, returning a denial instead of a connection — the act stage's network surface is policy-bound, not model-discretion-bound.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the net-policy collar around the browser/http nodes to see which destinations are inside the allowed ring.
touch_interaction.visual: Allowed URLs glow inside a green ring; a request to a private IP snaps against a red boundary and bounces back.

examples.mini_scenario: The model tries to fetch http://169.254.169.254; validate_url_target flags it as internal and the loop gets a denial ToolResult instead of metadata.
examples.pitfall: Validating the hostname but not its resolved IP lets DNS rebinding slip past the policy — check both.

examples.title: Capture the screen as verify evidence
examples.intent: Confirm a UI change actually rendered, not just that the code compiled.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ScreenCapture grabs the framebuffer and VisionAnalyze (encode_image_file + a vision-capable LLM) interprets it; the verify stage gains pixel-level evidence that complements cargo test's text-level pass/fail.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread over the ScreenCapture node to enlarge its screenshot into a full review card.
touch_interaction.visual: The node grows an image thumbnail with a camera badge; VisionCompare overlays a before/after split slider when a prior capture exists.

examples.mini_scenario: After editing a TUI widget, the loop captures the screen and VisionAnalyze confirms the new status bar actually renders.
examples.pitfall: Emitting raw base64 into the text log instead of the image slot bloats context and hides the picture from the vision model.

examples.title: Navigate code with LSP instead of grep guessing
examples.intent: Resolve definitions and references precisely where text search would over-match.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: create_lsp_tools wires an LspClientHandle into LspGotoDefinitionTool, LspFindReferencesTool, LspDocumentSymbolsTool and LspDiagnosticsTool; the loop perceives compiler-grade symbol truth and even live diagnostics, cutting the re-read churn that GrepSearch-only loops suffer.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a symbol chip on the canvas to fire LspGotoDefinitionTool; the camera flies to the resolved definition node.
touch_interaction.visual: A beam edge animates from the reference chip to the definition chip; LspDiagnosticsTool badges files with live error counts.

examples.mini_scenario: Instead of grepping 'render' and reading five false positives, the loop goto-definitions straight to the impl and edits it in one act.
examples.pitfall: Spawning LspClientHandle sessions without shutdown leaks language-server processes; wire shutdown into the loop's teardown.

examples.title: Budget an introspection run before diving in
examples.intent: Read a large codebase within a token ceiling instead of blowing the context window.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeIntrospect with TokenBudget (reserve/allocate/estimate_file/suggest_depth) plans how deep to parse each file; Depth downgrade kicks in when exhausted, and next_iteration paces multi-pass reads — the loop's perceive stage becomes budget-shaped rather than greedy.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the introspect node to reveal a budget gauge; drag the gauge to set the token ceiling before the dive starts.
touch_interaction.visual: The gauge fills as reserve/allocate consume budget; near exhaustion the node dims and Depth visibly downgrades file cards to brief.

examples.mini_scenario: Given 20k tokens, TokenBudget estimates 40 files, parses the hot eight at full depth, briefs the rest, and stops at the ceiling.
examples.pitfall: Parsing everything at full depth exhausts the budget on low-value files — let suggest_depth triage first.

examples.title: Rank code search with the BM25 query engine
examples.intent: Get the most relevant files first when the codebase is too big to read.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CodeQueryEngine::build_index parses the tree once; search and rank_files return RankedResult entries scored by BM25 over extract_keywords, and find_related_symbols expands from a hit — the perceive stage gets an ordered shortlist instead of an unordered flood.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick through the ranked result stack; the top card is the next file the loop will read.
touch_interaction.visual: Result cards stack by score with a relevance meter; higher scores sit brighter and closer to the camera.

examples.mini_scenario: Querying 'token budget enforcement' returns budget.rs ranked first; the loop reads it directly instead of scanning the module.
examples.pitfall: Searching against a stale index misses new files — rebuild_index after big mutation batches.

examples.title: Persist what the loop learns into the knowledge graph
examples.intent: Turn one-off discoveries into durable, queryable facts for later turns and runs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: KnowledgeAdd inserts a KnowledgeNode (typed by NodeType), KnowledgeRelate draws KnowledgeEdge relations, and KnowledgeQuery (find_by_type/find_by_name, edges_from/edges_to) recalls them — the loop's learn stage compounds instead of re-deriving the same facts every session.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge between two KnowledgeNode chips to assert a KnowledgeRelate relation.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes render as typed gems (file, symbol, decision); new edges spark and then settle into the graph's web.

examples.mini_scenario: After verifying that module X owns retry logic, the loop adds a node and relates it to the config module; a later run recalls it instantly.
examples.pitfall: Adding unverified guesses pollutes the graph — only persist facts that survived the verify stage.

examples.title: Hot-swap a tool without restarting the loop
examples.intent: Add or replace a tool implementation mid-run for experimentation.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: HotReloadManager::load/register builds a DynamicTool, get_tool/list_tools expose it, and reload swaps the implementation in place — the act stage's substrate is mutable, so tool fixes ship into a running loop instead of requiring a restart.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick a tool node upward to reload it; the node briefly phases out and returns with a version badge bump.
touch_interaction.visual: The node shimmers during reload; a green 'v+1' badge appears, or a red badge if load failed and the old impl kept serving.

examples.mini_scenario: A developer edits a custom tool's source, flicks reload, and the loop's next act turn uses the fixed implementation.
examples.pitfall: Reloading without re-registering in the ToolRegistry leaves the old schema in critical_definitions — sync both.

examples.title: Reorder the toolset by task focus
examples.intent: Present the model the tools that matter for this task type, first.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: classify_task maps the prompt to a TaskType; primary_tools and secondary_tools plus reorder_tools reshuffle the definitions list, and preamble primes the model — the reason stage sees a task-shaped toolset, improving tool choice without adding a single token of tools.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotate the tool shelf to re-sort nodes by task relevance; primary tools swing to the front of the rail.
touch_interaction.visual: Primary tools slide forward with a bright underline; secondary tools recede but stay reachable; irrelevant tools dim.

examples.mini_scenario: A debugging prompt classifies as debug; cargo_test and grep_search jump to the front of the tool list and the model picks them immediately.
examples.pitfall: Misclassification hides the actually-needed tool at the back — keep the full list reachable, only reorder.

examples.title: Ask the human one question instead of guessing
examples.intent: Resolve ambiguity with a single human answer rather than a speculative act batch.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ClarificationTool's ask_user suspends the act stage, surfaces one question, and resumes with the answer as evidence; asked_count caps how often the loop may interrupt, so clarification stays a deliberate control move, not a crutch.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the clarify node to open the pending question card; answering resumes the loop along a highlighted edge.
touch_interaction.visual: The loop dims behind a question card with a pulsing border; asked_count shows as remaining-interrupt pips on the node.

examples.mini_scenario: Unsure whether 'update' means deps or docs, the loop asks once, gets 'docs', and executes the right act batch first try.
examples.pitfall: Clarifying on every ambiguity burns asked_count and user patience — reserve it for forks that change the plan's shape.
